<action type="say">
Here’s what to do right now, then how to get someone out quickly.

1) Immediate steps (limit damage)
- Clear everything out from under the sink so nothing blocks access.  
- Put a bucket, bowl, or pan under the P-trap and where you see the drip.  
- If the drip is more than very slow, shut off water to the sink:  
  • Under-sink shutoffs: look for two small valves on the hot and cold lines; turn both clockwise until they stop.  
  • If that doesn’t stop it or valves are stuck, shut off the main water to the house if you know where it is.  
- Wipe up water in the cabinet so it doesn’t soak and warp the wood.

2) Lining up an emergency plumber in Fort Worth (since I can’t place the call directly)
On your phone/computer, search:
- “emergency plumber Fort Worth 76102” or  
- “24 hour plumber near 1234 Main Street Fort Worth”

Then:
- Focus on companies with rating ~4.5+ and at least dozens of reviews.  
- Make sure they say “24/7” or “emergency service” and show “open now.”  
- Call the top 2–3 directly (phone call, not just web forms) so you can confirm arrival time.

When you call, say something like:
- “I’m at 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, TX 76102.”  
- “I have a kitchen sink leak under the cabinet, a steady drip from the P-trap area, bottom of the cabinet is getting wet.”  
- “This is an emergency; I need someone out as soon as possible today.”  

Ask each one:
- “What is your emergency/trip fee?”  
- “What’s your hourly rate or flat fee for a P-trap/under-sink leak?”  
- “What’s the earliest you can get here?”  
- “Do you carry common P-trap parts and seals on the truck?”

Pick the one who can come soonest with clear pricing and good reviews.

If you want, paste 2–3 company names and their basic info (rating, fees, ETA), and I’ll help you pick quickly and suggest any questions to ask based on their listings or reviews.</action>
